title: Under the Silver Leaves
beat: The meadow becomes an intimate, hedgehog-sized world on the way to the elder.
camera: Place the camera 8 cm above the meadow soil beside the trail. Look through a loose arch of silver-backed leaves, with the route and distant knoll beyond.
staging: Keep the central opening clear for a small hedgehog walking through later.
alt: A low empty gap beneath silver-green leaves beside the woodland trail.

references.role: Location and framing reference; inspect before generation.

prompt: Move the camera off the reference's meadow path and down to just 8 cm above the soil at its edge, about 30 cm from a loose arch of broad silver-backed leaves. Look THROUGH that natural arch using a close wide 28mm view: detailed leaf veins and fine hairs at the upper edges, dark fresh soil below, a clear empty oval opening in the middle about 25 cm across. Beyond the opening we glimpse the winding trail and the same distant oak-crowned hill softly, without heavy blur. This is a tiny hedgehog-scale passage beside the trail, not a giant cave or a human-sized tunnel. Morning sun touches the translucent silver leaf edges from the right. Keep the middle opening and its ground unoccupied. Landscape-only environment plate: plants, soil, stone and sky, with no animals, birds, insects or characters. Warm dimensional children's-book woodland, soft natural highlights and detailed green shadows. Single landscape 1536x1024, no text or panels.
review: The low leaf-window camera has strong foreground parallax and clearly visible silver hairs and veins. The crown oak, base oak and approach trail remain recognizable beyond the opening. No fauna visible. The arch is more geometrically complete than an ordinary random leaf cluster, a storybook staging choice; scale must be checked when PinPin is added. Bright sunlit hairs approach white, but the leaf surfaces retain green texture.
